summary: This is a Docker Compose configuration for a Python application service. It defines how to build a development Docker image with Python, sets up environment variables for container configuration, and mounts volumes to persist VSCode extensions and bash history between container runs.

explanations.7: The 'target: development' tells Docker to build up to a specific stage in the Dockerfile called 'development', rather than building the entire file — useful when a Dockerfile has multiple stages for different purposes.
explanations.10: This passes the DOCKER_PYTHON_VERSION variable from your host environment into the Docker build process, where it's used to determine which Python version to install.
explanations.12: The syntax ${DOCKER_APP_HOME:-/app} means 'use the value of DOCKER_APP_HOME if it's set, otherwise default to /app' — it's a fallback mechanism.
explanations.21: This sets which user and group IDs the container will run as; the format is userid:groupid, and it uses the same defaults as the build arguments above.
explanations.27: The dot (.) represents your current directory on your host machine, and it gets mounted at the DOCKER_APP_HOME path inside the container, so code changes on your computer are instantly visible in the container.
explanations.29: This creates a named volume that persists VSCode server extensions across container restarts, so you don't have to reinstall extensions every time the container stops and starts.
